title: The inevitable
hookLine: the reality, what is the reality (69:1–3)

lines: THE SHORT LIST OF CERTAIN THINGS.
A SURAH NAMED FOR ONE OF THEM.
cards: Most of what fills a day isn't certain. The traffic might clear. The text might get a reply.
The weather app says forty percent. We spend hours on maybes. Now think of the short list of things that are not maybes.
The sun will set tonight. You were born. You will die.
Surah sixty-nine is named for one thing on that list that is easy to forget. It opens by saying its name, and then asking what it is, twice.

teach.h: THE REALITY! WHAT IS THE REALITY?
teach.b: Surah al-Haqqah begins, in Pickthall's translation: "The Reality! What is the Reality?" Then the third verse asks again: and what will make you know what the Reality is?
Al-haqqah comes from the root h-q-q, the root of haqq: truth, what is real, what is due, what must come to pass.

Translators reach for different words, the Reality, the Inevitable, the Sure Truth, because the Arabic holds all of them. One of the names of Allah, al-Haqq, the Truth, the Real, comes from the same root.

teach.h: NAME IT, ASK IT, ASK AGAIN.
teach.b: The opening is a teaching device the Qur'an uses more than once: name a thing, ask what it is, then ask how you could possibly know. And what is it?
Commentators read it as the Day of Resurrection, the day that is certain to come. But the surah doesn't open with a description.

teach.h: THE PEOPLES WHO SAID IT WASN'T.
teach.b: It goes straight into history: the peoples of 'Ad and Thamud, who called the coming day a lie, and what happened to them. Pharaoh. The flood in Nuh's time.
Before telling you about the day, the surah reminds you that people have been sure it wasn't coming for a very long time. The point isn't fear for its own sake. It's sorting.
Some things in your life are maybes. A few are haqq, real and due. The surah's opening is a call to tell them apart.

how: Muslims believe in the Last Day as one of the articles of faith; surahs like al-Haqqah, recited in prayer, are a regular reminder of it, and al-Haqq, the Truth, is one of the names of Allah.

o: al-Haqqah, the day certain to come, real and due
a disaster that strikes a people without warning
a feeling of dread about what tomorrow may bring

p: a name of Allah: the Real
peoples who said the day wasn't coming

s: al-Haqqah and al-Haqq share a root
h-q-q: what is true, real and due.
the surah opens with a full description of the Last Day
it asks what the Reality is, then turns to the peoples of the past.
commentators read al-haqqah as the Day of Resurrection
the day that is certain to come.

games.q: the surah has just named the Reality and asked, twice, what it is. what does it do next?
o: gives the date it will come.
tells of peoples who denied it.
games.why: it turns to history: 'Ad, Thamud, Pharaoh and the flood. people have been sure it wasn't coming for a long time.

practice: Let today's maybes come up, the worries, the plans, the waiting, and set each one to the side, as if on a shelf.

Then ask what's certain: that I'm breathing now, that this day will end, that my life will end too, one day, and, Muslims would add, that I'll be asked what I did with it. Stay with that short list, and notice how quiet it is.

wordCard.voice: The inevitable. Al-Haqqah, the Reality: the day that is certain to come, from the root of haqq, what is true and due. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Reality, the inevitable, from h-q-q, the root of haqq, truth.
